title: The Colour out of Space by H. P. Lovecraft

evidence.paraphrase: The construction of a reservoir will submerge the area, altering the landscape.
evidence.quotation: The new reservoir will soon be built now, and all those elder secrets will lie safe forever under watery fathoms.

evidence.paraphrase: The meteorite material is unusually malleable, described by scientists.
evidence.quotation: It was, in truth, so soft as to be almost plastic; and they gouged rather than chipped a specimen to take back to the college for testing.

evidence.paraphrase: Scientists performed laboratory tests on the meteorite using standard chemical procedures.
evidence.quotation: They tested it in a crucible with all the proper reagents. Water did nothing.

evidence.paraphrase: The meteorite traveled from space to Earth, landing near a well.
evidence.quotation: The meteorite fell out of the sky and bedded itself in the ground beside the well at the Nahum Gardner place.

evidence.paraphrase: The meteorite is believed to contaminate local agriculture, leading to future crop failures.
evidence.quotation: Nahum declared that the meteorite had poisoned the soil.

evidence.paraphrase: The meteorite's arrival caused a destructive event, killing people and damaging property.
evidence.quotation: The meteorite fell out of the sky and bedded itself in the ground beside the well at the Nahum Gardner place.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator leaves town after witnessing the strange events.
evidence.quotation: I hurried back before sunset to my hotel, unwilling to have the stars come out above me in the open; and the next day returned to Boston to give up my position.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrative contrasts normal pasture conditions with sudden deterioration.
evidence.quotation: The grass had so far seemed untouched, but the cows were freely pastured in the lot near the house, but toward the end of May the milk began to be bad.
